title: 1992 AMC 8 Problem 16
statement: Which cylinder has twice the volume of the cylinder shown at right?

solutions.text:
The given cylinder has volume \(\pi \times 10^2 \times 5 = 500\pi,\) so a cylinder of twice the volume has volume \(1000\pi.\)

The choices have volumes \(\pi \times 20^2 \times 5 = 2000\pi\) (A), \(\pi \times 10^2 \times 10 = 1000\pi\) (B), \(\pi \times 5^2 \times 20 = 500\pi\) (C), and \(\pi \times 20^2 \times 10 = 4000\pi\) (D). Only (B) equals \(1000\pi.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B .
hints: The volume of a cylinder is \(\pi r^2 h\); first compute the volume of the given cylinder
Doubling the height doubles the volume, but doubling the radius multiplies the volume by \(4\); check the \(r\) and \(h\) labels on each choice
